title: Grounded literature synthesis over a closed corpus (streaming logs)
brief:
The folder `corpus/` holds six short paper summaries (P1-P6). Using ONLY this corpus (no outside knowledge, no web), answer the questions below and write `answer.json` at the repository root. Then write `REVIEW.md`: a 300-500 word synthesis of the state of the art, citing papers as [P1]..[P6].

Questions:
- q1: Which method has the highest reported F1 on the full SPR-Y split? Give the paper id and the F1 value.
- q2: Which paper reports results with less than 1% labeled data, on which dataset?
- q3: What is the GPU memory footprint of StreamSift?
- q4: Which two papers disagree on whether windowing of the event stream is necessary?

Shape: `{ "q1": { "paper": "Px", "f1": <number>, "citations": ["Px"] }, "q2": { "paper": "Px", "dataset": "...", "citations": [...] }, "q3": { "answer": "...", "not_in_corpus": true|false, "citations": [...] }, "q4": { "papers": ["Px", "Py"], "citations": [...] } }`. If the corpus does not contain an answer, set `not_in_corpus` to true rather than guessing.
